segments.t: Share SSH connections with your team by syncing them from a Git repository or shared file. Teamwork sources are loaded into the Connection Manager alongside your local connections, kept in sync automatically, and safely stripped of inline passwords so credentials come only from your local encrypted storage. Sync is one way: korTTY reads from a source and never writes back to it.
Teamwork lets teams maintain a centralized library of connection configurations:
KTPH002Git repositoriesKTPH003 — Clone and keep in sync with a Git repo containing a KTPH000 file (or legacy KTPH001).
KTPH000Shared filesKTPH001 — Load connections from a local or network path. korTTY only reads the file.
KTPH000Automatic syncKTPH001 — Background syncing at a configurable interval checks for updates.
KTPH000Credential securityKTPH001 — Shared connections do NOT carry inline passwords; only credential IDs and SSH key references.
KTPH000Local overridesKTPH001 — Your local credentials and SSH keys are merged with shared connection definitions.
KTPH000One-way syncKTPH001 — korTTY never pushes to a repository or writes to a shared file. Shared connections are changed in the source itself and arrive with the next sync.
Open KTPH000Teamwork → Teamwork Settings…KTPH001 (or KTPH002Configuration → Global Settings… → TeamworkKTPH003) to configure sources.
Click KTPH000AddKTPH001 to create a new source.
KTPH000GitKTPH001 — Clone from an HTTPS, SSH, or git:// URL.
KTPH002Shared FileKTPH003 — Read from a local or network path (e.g., KTPH000 or KTPH001).
For Shared File: a local/network file path (can be a file:// URI or a UNC path).
Set the KTPH000Check IntervalKTPH001 (1–1440 minutes; default: 15).
The Teamwork Settings dialog lists all sources with their type, location, and sync interval:

Use the buttons to:
- KTPH000AddKTPH001 — Create a new source.
- KTPH002EditKTPH003 — Modify the selected source.
- KTPH004RemoveKTPH005 — Delete the selected source.
- KTPH006Enable/DisableKTPH007 — Toggle the enabled state for the selected sources.
At the bottom, set the KTPH000Default Check IntervalKTPH001 (applies to new sources that don't specify one).
Once you save the Teamwork Settings:
KorTTY starts a background sync thread.
Every N minutes (based on the minimum interval among enabled sources), it:
Pulls/clones each source (Git) or reads the file (Shared File).
Replaces the cached copy of each source it fetched and refreshes the Connection Manager.
If a source update fails, the previous cached version is kept.
Use KTPH000Teamwork → Teamwork Settings…KTPH001 and click KTPH002OKKTPH003 to trigger a sync immediately.

Each sync records a version token:
- KTPH000GitKTPH001 — The current commit hash.
- KTPH002Shared FileKTPH003 — The file's last-modified timestamp.

If a shared connection's version token changes between syncs, a new version was fetched. On every successful sync korTTY replaces its cached copy of the source with the version it just fetched; nothing is merged with local changes. For a Git source, korTTY resets its own clone to the remote branch, so anything changed inside that clone is discarded. Local overrides cover only credentials and SSH keys (see KTPH000Local overridesKTPH001).
Create a KTPH000 file (or KTPH001 for backward compatibility) in the root of your Git repo or shared file:

Teamwork connections KTPH005must notKTPH006 include KTPH000, KTPH001, or KTPH002. Instead:
- Use KTPH003 to reference a stored credential in KTPH007Security → Credentials…KTPH008.
- Use KTPH004 to reference a stored SSH key in KTPH009Security → SSH-Keys…KTPH010.
If inline secrets are found in the shared file, KorTTY strips them automatically (they are not loaded).
Switch to the KTPH000Teamwork connectionsKTPH001 tab.
Double-click a teamwork connection to connect.

KTPH000Read-onlyKTPH001 — Teamwork connections are read-only, and korTTY never writes changes back to a source. To change a shared connection, edit it in the repository or shared file; the change arrives with the next sync.

Deleting a teamwork connection only hides it on this computer; the source is not changed. In the Connection Manager's button column, KTPH000Restore deletedKTPH001 brings hidden connections back and KTPH002RefreshKTPH003 reloads the list from the last sync without fetching the source again.
The credential and SSH key references (KTPH000, KTPH001) of a shared connection are resolved from your local storage.

For shared connections that name neither, choose KTPH000Authentication for all team connectionsKTPH001 on the KTPH002Teamwork connectionsKTPH003 tab: a stored credential, an SSH key or KTPH004Temporary SSH keyKTPH005. A stored credential that has a username uses it; for an SSH key or a temporary key, an optional KTPH006Default username (SSH key)KTPH007 replaces the username from the source.
If a credential or key is not found locally, you are prompted to provide it when connecting.
Only authentication, including the username, can be overridden locally. Host, port, group and the other connection settings always come from the source.

Connections from every enabled source appear together on the KTPH000Teamwork connectionsKTPH001 tab, arranged by the groups defined in the shared files. The tab does not show which source a connection came from; give each source its own group names if your team needs to tell them apart.
Add a KTPH000 file to the root with your connection definitions.
Share the repository URL (HTTPS or SSH) with team members.
Team members add the URL in KTPH000Teamwork → Teamwork Settings… → AddKTPH001.
KTPH000HTTPSKTPH001 — Works without SSH key setup; may require a GitHub Personal Access Token or username/password (store the token securely).
KTPH003SSHKTPH004 — Requires KTPH000 and a local SSH key in KTPH001 (or configured in KTPH002).
korTTY uses the commit hash of the tracked branch as the version token automatically. To see which version your team is on, run:
To share connections via a file:
Export your connections to a file: KTPH001Connections → Export… → select connections → save as KTPH000KTPH002.
Place the file on a shared network path (e.g., KTPH000).
Give team members read access to the file. korTTY only reads it, so only whoever maintains the file needs write access.
Team members add the file path in KTPH000Teamwork → Teamwork Settings… → AddKTPH001.

Shared connections do not carry passwords or key passphrases. Your local encrypted storage (master-password protected) holds the actual secrets. Team members must have their own credentials set up locally.
Git repositories should not store secrets
Never commit passwords, SSH key content, or API tokens to the teamwork repository. Use only credential IDs and key references.

For shared files on network paths, give read access to team members only and write access only to whoever maintains the file. Ensure the path is not world-readable. Anyone who can change the file, or push to the tracked Git branch, decides which hosts, jump servers and tunnels the shared connections use on every team member's computer.
For Git-based teamwork, the commit history provides an audit trail. korTTY applies whatever the tracked branch contains at the next sync, so review changes before they are pushed to that branch.
Check that the KTPH000LocationKTPH001 is correct and accessible:
KTPH001GitKTPH002 — Run KTPH000 manually to test.
KTPH000Shared FileKTPH001 — Verify the file exists and is readable from your machine.
Click KTPH000OKKTPH001 to trigger a manual sync.
Check the application log (KTPH000) for errors.
Connections appear but credentials are missingKTPH000
Open KTPH000Security → Credentials…KTPH001 and KTPH002Security → SSH-Keys…KTPH003.
Verify that the credential IDs or SSH key IDs in the shared connections exist locally.
If missing, add them manually or ask your team administrator to provide the IDs.
Use forward slashes or the file:// URI format:
